_comment: What the canonical Notion tone-of-voice doc requires the linter to catch.
Notion is the source of truth for the RULES. This file is the machine-readable
extract of them, because .claude/hooks/voice_lint.py holds them as regexes and a
hook has to run fast and offline, so it cannot fetch Notion at write time. That
makes the regexes a copy, and copies drift.
scripts/check-voice-lint-coverage.mjs closes that loop: it feeds every term below
through the real hook and fails if the hook does not flag it. So Notion can gain a
banned word and CI will tell you the linter has not kept up.
TO REFRESH: read the Notion page (id 2ed3933a578d80d68233ca16390b9152) through the
Notion MCP connector, re-extract the spelling table and the never-list, update
mustFlag below, and bump sourceVersion. The check tests behaviour, not wording, so
adding a term here is what forces the linter to change.

mustNotFlag._comment: False positives are how a hook gets disabled and then enforces nothing. These must stay clean.

deliberateExclusions._comment: Notion bans these, but a regex cannot judge them without false positives. They stay a human/skill responsibility, and that is a decision rather than an oversight.
deliberateExclusions.leverage: Banned as a verb only. 'Leverage' as a noun is legitimate English and the regex cannot tell them apart.
deliberateExclusions.transform: Banned except for a literal data transformation, which is a real and common use in this product's copy.
deliberateExclusions.empower_note: Included above because the marketing sense dominates; if it starts firing on legitimate copy, move it here.
